Summary  
Data source overview: The appendix of an ICLR-2021 paper describes X2T, an adaptive text-entry system that learns a reward model from users’ implicit binary feedback (e.g., back-spaces) in three modalities: eye-gaze, on-screen handwriting, and an electrocorticography (ECoG) brain-computer interface (BCI). The appendix gives implementation details, ablation results and user-study findings that motivate several concrete design choices intended to make learning from noisy human feedback reliable and sample-efficient.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[86]  
Inference strategy justification: When sections provided only implementation detail, moderate inference (confidence 2) was used to elevate them to AI-safety–relevant causal claims (e.g., relating gradient-clipping to robustness). Otherwise edges rely on explicit empirical evidence (confidence 4).  
Extraction completeness explanation: All reasoning chains in the appendix that connect the central risk (“incorrect inference of user intent”) to concrete mitigations (offline pre-training, inductive biases, temporal-consistency filters, gradient clipping) are included and interconnected; no concept or intervention stands isolated.  
Key limitations: 1) Only appendix material was available; high-level motivations from the main paper were inferred. 2) Validation evidence for gradient-clipping is indirect (stable convergence claimed but not quantified). 3) Generalisation beyond text-entry modalities is not addressed here.
